question_text: What is glycogen? How is it different from starch?

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What glycogen is
lines: Glycogen is the carbohydrate stored in the
animal body, in the liver and in muscle.
It is also called animal starch.
It is a branched polymer of α-D-glucose.
steps.why: Glycogen does in an animal what starch does in a plant: it holds many glucose units in one insoluble molecule and release them on demand. Its heavy branching gives many chain ends, so glucose can be released quickly.
common_mistakes: Writing that glycogen is found in plants. It is the animal store; starch is the plant store.
Calling glycogen a polymer of β-D-glucose. Both starch and glycogen are built from α-D-glucose.
steps.memory_tip: Animal starch, stored in liver and muscle, heavily branched.
steps.margin_note: The words "animal starch" and "branched polymer of α-D-glucose" carry this mark.

steps.label: The difference from starch

lines.text: Starch has two parts; glycogen has one

lines: Starch is a mixture of two polymers:

lines.text: a) amylose, a linear polymer of α-D-glucose

steps.why: Both are α-D-glucose polymers, so the difference is not in the monomer or the linkage but in the make-up of the whole material: starch is two polymers together, one straight and one branched, while glycogen is a single, more heavily branched polymer.
common_mistakes: Writing that starch is a single polymer. It has two components, amylose and amylopectin.
Saying glycogen and starch differ in their linkage. Both use α-glycosidic linkages; only the branching differs.
steps.memory_tip: Starch is amylose plus amylopectin; glycogen is amylopectin taken further.
steps.margin_note: Name both parts of starch. The comparison to amylopectin is what completes the difference.

insider_note: Two things are being asked, so answer both: what glycogen is, then one clear difference. The difference the examiner is looking for is that starch has two components and glycogen has one.
